description:
## Verified problem

The `make_reducer` even/gt2 witness settles two semantic reducer activations. Each captured predicate is carried as `ValueRef` and invoked through an indirect `closure_call`. The semantic identities and the two predicate construction words are observable, but the completed native reducer/continuation graphs are otherwise equivalent. Before this ticket, both graphs were materialized and code-generated separately.

The direct-carrier control `mk(double)` / `mk(triple)` is different: its lambda bodies contain distinct grounded local targets. Those graphs must not share.

## Goal

Retain every semantic activation and runtime construction identity while compiling one physical native CPS graph for sibling activations whose complete native graphs are equivalent. The sharing pass must cost materially less work than the code generation it removes.

## Chosen boundary and strategy

`NativeProgram` is the ownership boundary. `BackendProgram` remains the interpreter's semantic/index authority; merging there would erase semantic identity or require a parallel remap before native ABI, direct targets, construction words, and the complete CPS graph are explicit. No existing canonical key is suitable: `IrFn` equality includes owned function/name/callsite allocation identities, backend canon is comparison-only and world/string based, and the JIT has no linker-level identical-code folding.

`NativeProgram.executable_entries` therefore keeps one `ExecutableKey -> FnId` row per semantic executable while permitting several rows to name one physical entry. After lowering completes, each fixed-point pass builds one ephemeral ownership index from existing `NativeBodyOrigin` facts. Siblings are compared in canonical root/clause/owner-local-continuation roles. Continuation indices are minted within their owner; global numbering remains diagnostic-name identity only. Duplicate body, clause, continuation, or graph roles are invariant failures, never silently collapsed.

Comparison alpha-renames only graph-owned `FnId`s, diagnostic function names, and same-span callsite allocation identities. Direct targets, construction words, ABI/repr facts, effects, captures, extern marshals, and other codegen-relevant types compare exactly. A type may differ only for a `ValueRef` variable exhaustively proven by the IR-use walk to occur solely as the callee word of an indirect closure call.

Every accepted mapping rewrites the module entry, semantic entry map, callable-boundary target functions, continuation owners, and CPS control edges; removes the redundant bodies/functions; and rebuilds the module function index. Construction-producing IR is not remapped.

## Measured signal on current base 21711b335

The deterministic 502-candidate census reaches 467 native programs and 465 paired codegen successes. It finds 662 same-function sibling groups and 40 equivalent classes. Sharing preserves 5,338 semantic entries and 148 `MakeClosure` instructions while reducing:

- physical roots: 5,338 -> 5,281 (-57)
- continuations: 8,356 -> 8,220 (-136)
- all native bodies: 14,989 -> 14,796 (-193)
- native text: 3,483,036 -> 3,438,764 bytes (-44,272)

Two identical corrected runs repeat exactly: 488 ownership-index passes, 19,599 indexed bodies, 17,476 owned graph-body roles, 4,751 graph comparisons, and 4,621 body comparisons. Sharing took 82.321 ms and 53.532 ms; paired codegen savings were 1,051 ms and 524 ms, so sharing remained about 13x and 10x cheaper.

The rejected scan design did 4,924 graph comparisons, varied between 5,659 and 5,698 body comparisons across identical runs, and spent about 1,516 ms while avoiding about 1,179 ms of codegen. It is not the accepted design.

## Acceptance

- The exact even/gt2 reducer matches Elixir on interp, JIT, and AOT.
- The boxed pair begins as disjoint complete graphs, differs only at proven indirect-callee `ValueRef` types, retains both semantic activations and predicate construction words, and maps to one physical graph.
- Changing an owner-local continuation index makes two otherwise equal graphs inequivalent; duplicate ownership roles fail explicitly.
- `mk(double)` / `mk(triple)` retains two physical graphs and distinct grounded targets.
- Dynamic callable-construction, capture-layout, recursive-search telemetry, semantic-to-physical movement, and all current-base behavior remain green.
- The retained census reproduces the classified population and exact reductions above with deterministic work counts and no unexplained behavior movers.
- No test requires duplicate bodies.
- `cargo fmt --check`, strict all-target/all-feature clippy, `cargo test --lib`, `cargo test --test fz2_cli`, and the complete fixture matrix pass.

## Composition with open work

PR #113 changes only wording near native lowering and deletes orphaned semantic closure state; it does not own native graph mapping. PR #110 changes upstream semantic/dispatch inputs and may shrink the executable population, but it does not touch `artifact.rs` or `jobs/native.rs`; this pass consumes whatever closed `BackendProgram` it receives and conservatively rejects any newly inequivalent graph. Corpus totals must be remeasured if that upstream arc lands first.

comments.text: Reopened during cumulative current-base review: the original normalized comparer saved 44,272 emitted bytes but temporary census instrumentation measured 4,924 graph / 5,698 body comparisons across 488 passes and ~1.516s sharing cost versus ~1.179s codegen reduction, with a ~586ms worst case and hash/early-exit-dependent comparison counts. This violates the arc performance goal. Retain the native ownership boundary, but replace repeated full-body scans with deterministic indexed/canonical ownership (or a simpler measured equivalent), remove probes, and re-run exact output/work/behavior gates before cold review and delivery.

title: Boxed captured-callable specializations duplicate native CPS bodies despite distinct semantic identities
